summary.headline: Shanti Gold Q1 FY27 revenue rose 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores, with PAT of INR50.48 crores, though management flagged about 2-2.5 points of EBITDA margin from one-off inventory gains.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores and PAT rose 46.94% to INR50.48 crores, with PAT margin at 7.05%. EBITDA was INR71.45 crores at a 9.97% margin, which management said includes roughly 2-2.5 percentage points of unrealised inventory gain from the FIFO-to-WAC change. Management guided to 7.5-8% EBITDA margin going forward, reiterated FY27 guidance of 50-60% value growth and 30-40% volume growth (about INR3,500 crores revenue), and said the Marol (Mumbai) plant commenced operations in June 2026. A INR100 crore rights issue was approved to fund working capital and growth.

+39% YoY vs INR51.41 crores in Q1 FY26
Management plans to take it up to below 1x

segments.name: Studded jewellery
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of jewellery sold is studded; in a separate answer it said 75% of revenue is designer jewellery and 25% plain gold, and about 75% is cast-studded. The figures given during the call are inconsistent and need clarification.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery
segments.commentary: Management cited about 30% of jewellery sold as plain gold, or 25% of revenue, in different answers.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 4% of Q1 revenue. A Dubai office is awaiting RBI approval; management described it as the base for international expansion, currently serving three to four countries.

guidance_outlook: FY27 value growth guidance of 50-60% YoY, equal to a revenue target of about INR3,500 crores; management said it could revise upward if Q3 demand is strong.
FY27 volume growth guidance of 30-40% YoY. Management called a repeat of the roughly 61-62% Q1 volume growth 'wishful thinking'.
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 7.5-8% for FY27 after removing the 2-2.5 point inventory gain; management said margin could move toward 10% over three to four years as new facilities scale.
Jaipur facility to start around mid-November or December 2026, with capex of about INR47 crores.
Management expects working capital needs to rise and plans a debt/equity mix that stays below 1x, funded by debt plus the INR100 crore rights issue.
capex_capacity: Marol (Mumbai) manufacturing facility began operations in June 2026, with a new 4,000 kg-capacity line that is ramping up; management said it is a different jewellery line from the existing plant.
Existing Mumbai plant capacity is about 2,700 kg and is running at about 75% utilisation.
Jaipur facility capex is about INR47 crores; first phase is 50,000 sq ft on a 3-acre site, expected to add about 1,200 kg. Operations are targeted for mid-November to December 2026.
Rights issue of 46,43,471 equity shares of INR10 face value, aggregating up to INR100 crores; the issue opened on the day of the call. Post-issue share count is about 7.67 crore shares.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was about 61-62% YoY in Q1, driven by new designs, new customers and new markets. Management said gold was in a narrow INR142-150 band in FY27 and that May-June were subdued.
Gold prices rallied again in the weeks before the call following the IIJS exhibition; management said its long-term view on gold is very bullish.
Management said the exchange-programme trend in retail does not affect its demand.
Management said North India was recently entered and most northern clients are new; it said North and South margins are broadly similar.
Management said demand is strong after exhibitions, with orders in hand for export and domestic markets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin trajectory and gold price views?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about 4% PAT margin and 7.5-8% EBITDA margin. It said gold was in a narrow band, with a strong long-term view on gold.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume grew about 61% YoY in Q1, and FY27 volume guidance is 30-40% against value guidance of 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other expenses up 132% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects indirect expenses to support growth, not hedging losses, and that it is comparable to the scale of growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and the Jaipur capex?
qa_highlights.answer: The Mumbai plant is at about 75% utilisation. Jaipur capex is about INR47 crores, with operations expected around mid-November to December.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for negative operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds ready stock rather than producing order-to-order, so cash is tied up in inventory. Cash flow would turn positive only on an order-to-order model.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rights issue be used to add borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rights issue proceeds will go into gold inventory and working capital, and it will keep existing borrowings without taking new ones at this stage. It also said it expects to add both debt and equity over time.

risks_watch: Roughly 2-2.5 points of Q1 EBITDA margin came from a one-time inventory gain after the FIFO-to-WAC change. Underlying margin is 7.5-8%, so Q2 margin will show the true run-rate.

Working capital intensity is rising with 50-60% value growth guidance, a stock-heavy model and a debt/equity target below 1x from 0.50x. Management said cash flow from operations has been negative for several years.
Management said it uses gold metal loans only selectively; hedging policy and the share of GML-backed inventory were not clearly quantified.
Jaipur commissioning timeline (mid-Nov to Dec 2026) and Marol ramp-up are critical to the FY27 volume target.
Export share is small at 4% and the Dubai office is still awaiting RBI approval.
Management's answers on product mix (studded versus plain share) were inconsistent across the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on volumes and capacity, but cautious on margins and the sustainability of the Q1 profit. Management was vague on several numerical details (product mix, North/South split, gold hedging) and deferred some answers to year-end.
key_quotes: So roughly 2% to 2.5% was the inventory gain.
So the long-term, our vision towards the gold is very, very bullish.
The reason for being negative cash flow is like, we utilize all the funds and we keep the stock readily.
